content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching, the lamp most commonly symbolizes God's Word (Scripture) as a source of guidance and illumination for the believer's life, and by close extension the light of divine truth and witness that believers are to display to the world.", "primary_basis": ["Psalm 119:105 ('Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path')", "Proverbs 6:23 ('For the commandment is a lamp, and the teaching a light')", "2 Peter 1:19 (the prophetic word 'as a lamp shining in a dark place')", "Matthew 5:14-16 (a lamp is put on a stand to give light; 'let your light shine before others')", "Mark 4:21-22 / Luke 8:16 and Luke 11:33 (a lamp is not hidden under a basket or bed)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Christian witness or testimony: the believer's visible good works and gospel proclamation shining before others (often merged with the primary meaning in preaching).", "basis": ["Matthew 5:14-16", "Philippians 2:15", "Luke 12:35 ('keep your lamps burning')"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Spiritual readiness, watchfulness, and preparedness for Christ's return, especially via the oil supply in the lamp.", "basis": ["Matthew 25:1-13 (parable of the ten virgins)", "Luke 12:35-36"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "The churches themselves as lampstands bearing Christ's light; removal of the lampstand as loss of standing or witness.", "basis": ["Revelation 1:12-20 ('the seven lampstands are the seven churches')", "Revelation 2:5"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "The Holy Spirit, symbolized by burning lamps or the sevenfold lamps before God's throne; also linked to the tabernacle menorah kept perpetually burning.", "basis": ["Revelation 4:5 ('seven lamps of fire... which are the seven Spirits of God')", "Zechariah 4:1-6 (lampstand vision: 'not by might... but by my Spirit')", "Exodus 25:31-40; 27:20-21 (the golden lampstand and perpetual oil)"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "The human spirit or conscience as the inward faculty by which God illuminates a person.", "basis": ["Proverbs 20:27 ('The spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD')"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Dynastic continuity and covenant hope: the 'lamp of David' as the perpetuity of David's royal line, fulfilled messianically in Christ.", "basis": ["2 Samuel 21:17 ('the lamp of Israel')", "1 Kings 11:36; 15:4", "2 Kings 8:19", "Psalm 132:17"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "The eye as the 'lamp of the body,' representing moral perception, generosity, or singleness of devotion.", "basis": ["Matthew 6:22-23", "Luke 11:34-36"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Life itself, whose extinguishing signifies death or judgment on the wicked ('the lamp of the wicked is put out').", "basis": ["Job 18:5-6; 21:17", "Proverbs 13:9; 20:20; 24:20"], "prominence": "rare"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "The lamp is a well-attested, multivalent biblical image, but there is a recognizable dominant strand: God's Word/divine truth giving guidance (Ps 119:105 is among the most quoted verses on the theme), closely paired homiletically with the believer's duty to shine as a witness (Matt 5:14-16). Context strongly determines which sense applies: eschatological readiness in Matthew 25, ecclesial identity in Revelation 1, dynastic promise in Kings, and the Spirit in Zechariah 4 and Revelation 4. Lamp (portable oil vessel) and lampstand (menorah) are related but sometimes distinguished in scholarly treatment; popular teaching often conflates them."}
